note: Attacker-controlled NCP input (SPINEL_PROP_THREAD_ON_MESH_NETS value) registers an on-mesh prefix entry in mOnMeshPrefixes; because it is ON_MESH|SLAAC with /64, a SLAAC unicast address derived from it is stored in mUnicastAddresses with origin kOriginThreadNCP.
A later full-list ON_MESH_NETS update omits the previously reported prefix; the stale NCP-origin entry in the on_mesh_prefixes copy drives on_mesh_prefix_was_removed().

The matching OnMeshPrefixEntry is erased from mOnMeshPrefixes; entry.is_on_mesh() && entry.is_slaac() && prefix.get_length()==kSLAACPrefixLength && !has_slaac_on_mesh_prefix(prefix) is true, so the SLAAC-address cleanup branch is entered.
Locates the NCP-origin SLAAC unicast address whose /64 prefix matches the removed prefix inside mUnicastAddresses.
address becomes a const reference to the key object (struct in6_addr) stored inside the mUnicastAddresses std::map node.
The map-key reference is forwarded to unicast_address_was_removed(), which operates on it by reference.

mUnicastAddresses.erase(address) destroys the map node whose key the still-live reference `address` points into - the object is deleted while a reference to it remains in use below (use-after-delete).
remove_address(&address, ...) dereferences the dangling reference (origin is kOriginThreadNCP), reading from freed memory - the use-after-delete sink (ASan heap-use-after-free read).
